answer: Since the dune verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the jetty audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, since the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own beacon path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 6 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 6 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
